original.description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design a satellite system for FRMCS which is operating in the same frequency bands as the terrestrial counterpart (i.e., 900 MHz and 1.9 GHz), with the purpose to exclusively service the coverage gaps of the terrestrial network while avoiding interference. The performance of such system will be evaluated with the development of a system simulator.Targeted Improvements: - Reduce by 80% the cost of the satellite system for FRMCS.- Reduce by 50% the cost of on-board railway terminals, by allowing a single terminal solution for terrestrial and satellite FRMCS connectivity.Description: The Future RailwayMobile Communication System (FRMCS), being a successor of the GSM-R system, is planned to be operational before GSM-R's predicted saturation in 2030. Through standardisation work, satcom is established as a component of the future system, while it is found that the satellite integration into FRMCS is simplified when satcom is employing the 5G NR, which is the selected air interface for the terrestrial FRMCS access. However, the frequency bands for such a service via satellite and the design of the satellite system are yetto be concluded. The advantages of an innovative approach, where the satellite offers connectivity exclusively to the coverage gapsofsuch terrestrial network, have been recently reported. In fact, such a satellite system targeting only the terrestrial coverage gaps while ignoring the areas serviced by theterrestrial network, will have a lower complexity and overall cost, as fewer satellites of less capacity will be required. In addition, such a satellite system will be able to operate in the same frequency bands as theterrestrial network (i.e., 900 MHz and 1.9 GHz), as each network (terrestrial or satellite) will not be available in the same area where the other network operates and therefore they will not interfere with each other. This usage of the same frequency from the satellite and the terrestrial network not only facilitates the integration of the two networks into FRMCS, but also potentially allow the usage of the same terminal for both networks, a solution that is very favourable for railway operators. This activity will thereforeinvestigate the design of a 5G NR based satellite system for FRMCS which exclusively targets the terrestrial network gaps of communication and operates in the same frequency bands as the terrestrial FRMCS network. The activity will include a traffic characterisation and capacity analysis for the terrestrial network gaps which will then feed the system design and the element sizing of the ground and space components. The impact of the railway-satellite channel for the 900 MHz and the 1900 GHz will also be thoroughly investigated. The best numerologies and 5G NR configurations will also be identified for such a satellite system. The work will be supported by the development of a system simulator which will investigate the FRMCS 5G NR satellite link performance and achieved C/I ratios under a variety of different orbits, system architectures, frequency bands, channel conditions and air interface configurations. The activity will also investigate and conclude on the feasibility of having a single modem and a single antenna equipped on board the trains, which offer connectivity both to the satellite and the terrestrial network at different time instances.

original.description: As part of the Greek National Satellite Space Project - Phase 2, the objective of this activity is the procurement of Phase A/B1 for an In-Orbit Demonstration (IOD) mission aimed at the development and in-space demonstration of a flexible small-satellite platformenabling future In-Space Servicing, Assembly and Manufacturing (ISAM) missions.The mission shall demonstrate autonomous rendezvous,inspection and close-proximity operations (CPO) capabilities in orbit, while supporting the development of European industrial andcommercial capabilities and fostering future operational services.The mission shall address identified user needs and market opportunities with the objective of contributing to the development of future European in-space infrastructure and services. Tenderers shall therefore propose a mission concept that combines technology demonstration objectives with a credible path towards future operational applications.The mission and system development approach shall be based on a modular and scalable architecture, supported byanincremental demonstration strategy with clearly defined primary and extended objectives. The proposed implementation shall prioritise mission success, schedule robustness and affordability, while enabling future capability growth. Primary objectives will focus on demonstrating autonomous rendezvous, inspection and close-proximity operations capabilities, including relative navigation, guidance and control, onboard autonomy, mission operations and payload-carrying capability. Secondary objectives may include extended CPO manoeuvres (V-bar and R-bar approaches), synchronised relative motion demonstrations, technology maturation activities for futureISAM missions, and payload accommodation demonstrations such as advanced sensors or robotics. The implementation of secondary objectives will be subject to available resources and mission opportunities, without compromising the achievement of the primary objectives.

title: GREEK NATIONAL SATELLITE SPACE PROJECT - SPACE DOMAIN AWARENESS IN-ORBIT SERVICING (ISOS) PILLAR 2 - PHASE A/B1
description: As part of the Greek National Satellite Space Project - Phase 2, the objective of this activity is the procurement of Phase A/B1 for an In-Orbit Demonstration (IOD) mission aimed at the development and in-space demonstration of a flexible small-satellite platformenabling future In-Space Servicing, Assembly and Manufacturing (ISAM) missions.The mission shall demonstrate autonomous rendezvous,inspection and close-proximity operations (CPO) capabilities in orbit, while supporting the development of European industrial andcommercial capabilities and fostering future operational services.The mission shall address identified user needs and market opportunities with the objective of contributing to the development of future European in-space infrastructure and services. Tenderers shall therefore propose a mission concept that combines technology demonstration objectives with a credible path towards future operational applications.The mission and system development approach shall be based on a modular and scalable architecture, supported byanincremental demonstration strategy with clearly defined primary and extended objectives. The proposed implementation shall prioritise mission success, schedule robustness and affordability, while enabling future capability growth. Primary objectives will focus on demonstrating autonomous rendezvous, inspection and close-proximity operations capabilities, including relative navigation, guidance and control, onboard autonomy, mission operations and payload-carrying capability. Secondary objectives may include extended CPO manoeuvres (V-bar and R-bar approaches), synchronised relative motion demonstrations, technology maturation activities for futureISAM missions, and payload accommodation demonstrations such as advanced sensors or robotics. The implementation of secondary objectives will be subject to available resources and mission opportunities, without compromising the achievement of the primary objectives.

original.description: Objective:To implement, validate and test a cryptographic device for security protection of TC/TM.Description:Security protection of TC/TM utilizing cryptographic device capability shall be compliant with correspondingCCSDS standards, implementing SDLS (SpaceData Link Security protocol) and SDLS EP (ExtendedProcedures). It will also include the development of the corresponding Ground Segment Key Management module (unless the needed ground segment capability is already available through COTS or other developments). The implementation will be on hardware; software implementations (not part of this activity) can complement the development for smallsatellites with low assurance requirements or cubesats. The device will target the protection of TC and TM communication links.Theactivity will develop an engineering model, using a hardware based optimised implementations ofauthenticated encryption. Specifically, it will develop:- Engineering Model (EM): flight representative hardware in form, fit and function (including timing and interfaces), allowing functional qualification.- Unit tester / testbench (hardware) that allows to send data to the EM through any of its interfaces up to themaximum data rates supported by the EM (this includes encryption/decryption of data sent/received to the EM).Unit tester / testbench will also record data sent and received to the module.- Ground key management module (software) being ableto manage the cryptographic parameters and keys of the unit tester and EM.

original.description: This feasibility study shall analyse Canadian space weather assets including measurement, modelling and service provision capabilities and carry out initial pre-developments demonstrating these assets potential incorporation into the ESA Space Weather Service Network. Assets providing data access to be reviewed shall include both space and ground-based sensors along with data archives and repositories.Available assets shall be reviewed in terms of the Space Safety Programme's space weather customer and service requirements baseline along with the current level of service provided by the existing Space Weather Service Network in order to highlight priority areas where Canadian assets are expected to bring substantial capability enhancements. Consideration shall be given to the development planning prepared by the five Expert Service Centres participating in the network to ensure complementarity.Recommendations shall include identification of a set of high priority product development activities in key areas highlighting the potential contribution of Canadian space weather assets and capabilities both alone and in combination with other existing or potential SWE Service Network participants. Predevelopment shall take place in order to produce a set of representative product mock-ups. The first products shall be foreseen for integration into the SWE Service Network within the 2026 timeframe.
